title: Dipsomania, childhood and hereditary drinking
summary: Freeman distinguishes a dipsomaniac from a drunkard, says Tough could not handle one drink, and wonders whether childhood shapes later life.

story.theme_name: Drink, drugs and the bandstand's casualties
story.community_name: Drugs and drink on the bandstand and the road

blocks.x: A dipsomaniac is a man who can smell a cork and go completely berserk. Dave Tough was not a big drinker. He would take one drink and he was gone, out of his mind. But let's --
Well, would you say any of that is hereditary?

I just don't really know. As I say, if we could only know, so much of this may -- the child's mind is like a camera, it photographs pictures that can neither do well for it or destroys it as it goes on in life.

And at the age of three, we might make all our decisions. I don't know. But Dave Tough was just another profound guy and I found with profound people -- Bix was a profound man, with profound people such as poets, sculptors, sculptures, painters, writers, whatever the case may be, if I may say all sick -- we are all sick, aren't we?
